Tutor request: review this fictional deidentified complete cycle 1 run, including its opening and close. Player and Counterpart are the only speakers. No cue or coaching was used.
P1 Player: Closing after five days may make customers think we have stopped helping. I do not know how replies to closed tickets are handled. What happens when they reply?
C1 Counterpart: The ticket reopens in its original queue place.
P2 Player: That means they do not lose queue access. My concern remains whether the email makes them think we have refused to help. Queue access is settled; the meaning of the email is still uncertain.
C2 Counterpart: We need the general rule live Friday.
P3 Player: Friday is a deadline priority. Whether customers understand the email remains an evidence question.
C3 Counterpart: I will own an email revision.
P4 Player: Then we revise the closing email. You own the revision by Thursday. If complaints about closure rise above this week's count, we review the wording. Is that agreed?
C4 Counterpart: Agreed. I own that revision and review condition.

Public context supplied by tutor: The Counterpart has authority to edit and release the closing email and has a reserved editing slot before Thursday. No other supplied constraint conflicts with the revision.
